{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-ooyg","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-worker6-jjhj: Ack::from_bytes_for OOB panic on complete ACK","description":"## Critical panic bug

`Ack::from_bytes_for` (fragment.rs:300) unconditionally accesses `data[2]` after only checking `data.len() >= 2`. A complete ACK is exactly 2 bytes (`[rule_id, (window << 7) | 0x40]`), so when `FragmentSender::handle_ack_bytes` receives a complete ACK via `Ack::from_bytes(data)`, it panics with index out of bounds at `data[2]`.

## Root cause

`from_bytes_for` (line 307) reads `let n = data[2] as usize` before any length check that distinguishes complete vs non-complete ACKs. The complete flag is decoded at line 306 but never used to gate the subsequent bitmap parsing.

## How to reproduce

```rust
let complete_ack = [0x78, 0xc0]; // Complete ACK for window 1
let ack = Ack::from_bytes(&complete_ack); // PANICS: index 2 out of bounds
```

## Impact

Any reception path that calls `Ack::from_bytes` with a complete ACK will crash the sender. This happens when `FragmentSender::handle_ack_bytes` receives a complete ACK after successful reassembly.

## Fix needed

`Ack::from_bytes_for` must check the complete flag early and return a 2-byte complete ACK before attempting to read `data[2]`.

Related: the complete flag is read from bit 0 (`data[1] & 0x01`) but `write_to` places the complete marker at bit 6 (`0x40`). These don't match.","status":"open","priority":0,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T17:25:20.374492451Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T17:25:20.374492451Z"}
